hints: At constant speed on a level road, acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F_D$ equals the resistance: $F_D = 850\text{ N}$.
Calculate the power using $P = F_D \times v$.
Convert the result from watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$.
walkthrough:
State the equilibrium of forces along the direction of motion for constant speed on a level road ($a = 0$):
$$F_D = R$$
Given resistance $R = 850\text{ N}$, the driving force is $F_D = 850\text{ N}$.

State the power formula relating driving force and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $F_D = 850\text{ N}$ and $v = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 850 \times 36 = 30600\text{ W}$$

Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{30600}{1000} = 30.6\text{ kW}$$

hints: At constant speed up the hill, the driving force balances both the resistance and the component of weight down the slope: $F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$.
Calculate the required driving force using $m = 1250\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin\theta = 0.1$, and $R = 850\text{ N}$.
Use the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with $P = 63000\text{ W}$ to solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
State the force balance for uphill motion at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$$
where $F_D$ is the driving force, $R = 850\text{ N}$ is the resistance, and $mg\sin\theta$ is the downhill component of gravity.

Substitute the known values ($m = 1250\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin\theta = 0.1$):
$$mg\sin\theta = 1250 \times 10 \times 0.1 = 1250\text{ N}$$
Compute total driving force:
$$F_D = 850 + 1250 = 2100\text{ N}$$

State the power formula relating driving force and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v \implies v = \frac{P}{F_D}$$
Convert power to watts: $P = 63\text{ kW} = 63000\text{ W}$.
Substitute into the velocity equation:
$$v = \frac{63000}{2100} = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Apply the work-energy principle: $\text{Work done by engine} + \text{Loss in PE} = \text{Gain in KE} + W_{\text{res}}$.
Calculate the work done by the engine in $8\text{ s}$: $W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t = 20000 \times 8$.
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy: $\Delta E_p = mgh = mg(d\sin\theta)$, where $d = 176\text{ m}$.
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2)$, then solve for $W_{\text{res}}$.
walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for motion with external driving power and resistive forces:
$$W_{\text{engine}} + E_{p,\text{loss}} = E_{k,\text{gain}} + W_{\text{res}}$$
where $W_{\text{res}}$ is the work done against resistive forces.

Calculate the work input from the engine running at constant power $P = 20\text{ kW} = 20000\text{ W}$ for $t = 8\text{ s}$:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = P \times t = 20000 \times 8 = 160000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy as the car travels distance $d = 176\text{ m}$ down the slope of inclination $\sin\theta = 0.1$:
$$\text{Vertical drop}: \quad h = d\sin\theta = 176 \times 0.1 = 17.6\text{ m}$$
$$E_{p,\text{loss}} = mgh = 1250 \times 10 \times 17.6 = 12500 \times 17.6 = 220000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the gain in kinetic energy from $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k,\text{gain}} = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 1250 \times (24^2 - 20^2)$$
$$24^2 - 20^2 = 576 - 400 = 176$$
$$E_{k,\text{gain}} = 625 \times 176 = 110000\text{ J}$$

Substitute all quantities into the work-energy balance equation:
$$160000 + 220000 = 110000 + W_{\text{res}}$$
$$380000 = 110000 + W_{\text{res}}$$
Subtract $110000$ from both sides:
$$W_{\text{res}} = 380000 - 110000 = 270000\text{ J} = 270\text{ kJ}$$
